scope: Static public source only; no account/session/device/key operations. Nine new exact public assets acquired after one anonymous same-browser code-loader response. No official JavaScript executed.

consumer.keyFlow: waitForWormEarKey -> getWormEarKey -> openWAWormQueueDatabase(encKey) -> makeWAWormEarSyncDriver -> new WormEarSync(schema, alias, masterKey, options)

stateFamilies.role: pending local add-on deletion for parent message keys
pending sync-key share action; entity can contain keyData

consumer.scopeLimit: This is the only direct getWormEarKey callsite found in all reviewed source variants. It proves this consumer, not absence of other future/conditional consumers. It does not identify media-cache encryption.

masterDerivation.base: nonextractable HKDF CryptoKey with deriveBits usage; generated from 128 random bytes
masterDerivation.derived: HKDF SHA-256, salt decoded companion_enc_static, info UTF-8 worm-ear-v1, 256 output bits
masterDerivation.readiness: waitForWormEarKey can resolve after derivation error; getWormEarKey still throws if missing. generateFinalDbEncryptionAndFtsKey itself resolves before async derivations finish.

keychain.salt: random secretbox nonce concatenated with secretbox(random 32-byte salt, nonce, 32-byte master key)
keychain.keyHash: first 5 characters of Base64(SHA-256(master)); diagnostic comparison, not standalone cryptographic integrity
keychain.versionKey: HKDF SHA-256(clientKey, unwrapped salt, Binary.build(UTF-8 worm-ear-v2, one uint8 version), 32 bytes)
keychain.rotation: prepareNewKeyVersion uses default TTL 6*30*24*3600 seconds; init/resetKeyChain accepts ordered versions; latest numerical version used to encrypt
keychain.extraStore: _worm_db_version_ stores schema_hash and creation_ts; driver computes SHA-256(JSON.stringify(application schema plus system schema))

recordFormat.envelope: Binary.build(format byte 1, uint8 key version, fresh secretbox nonce, secretbox(MessagePack entity, nonce, version key))
recordFormat.primitive: WACryptoPrimitives.secretbox export through cr:8712; reviewed corpus contains tweetnacl-fast wrapper / tweetnacl-1.0.3-fast with 32-byte key, 24-byte nonce and 16-byte overhead. Runtime binding/shape must still be checked by any compatibility adapter.
recordFormat.encoding: WormEncoding MessagePack, ignoreUndefined:true; custom extension tags 0 ArrayBuffer, 1 Uint8Array, 2 BigInt as decimal string, 3 Set
recordFormat.indexing: Primary/index fields copied outside ciphertext. Numeric keys pass through; other encrypted fields use HMAC-SHA256(master, MessagePack(field)). nonEncryptedFields bypass hashing; ordered queueId remains clear. Full entity, including its original IDs, is inside ciphertext.
recordFormat.versionLimits: Binary.build encodes numbers with writeUint8; versions outside uint8 range cannot be silently coerced. Decrypt reads second envelope byte; adapter should validate exact supported envelope/schema.

internalAPIs.name: new WormEarSync(schema, dbAlias, masterKey, options)
internalAPIs.effect: in-memory crypto object; verifies master byteLength equals secretbox.keyLength

internalAPIs.name: ear.init(versionRecords, {eventFlow?})
internalAPIs.effect: unwraps version salts and builds in-memory version keys; no database access in method

internalAPIs.name: ear.maybeDecrypt(record, store, reason, eventFlow?, options?)
internalAPIs.effect: decrypts known secure entity; throws malformed/missing key/decryption error

internalAPIs.name: ear.maybeEncrypt(entity, store, eventFlow?)
internalAPIs.effect: fresh nonce encryption and primary/index field hashing

internalAPIs.name: ear.prepareNewKeyVersion()
internalAPIs.effect: generates new random clientKey, wrapped salt, expiration and short key hash; caller assigns version

internalAPIs.name: WormIDbStore.readAll/readIndex/readByKeyRange
internalAPIs.effect: decrypt through maybeDecrypt; called under driver transaction

internalAPIs.name: WormIDbStore.bulkPut/bulkAdd
internalAPIs.effect: encrypt through maybeEncrypt before IDB write

internalAPIs.name: WormDatabase.runInTransaction(stores, mode, callback, operationName)
internalAPIs.effect: per-database transaction; no cross-database snapshot guarantee

unsafeForBackupInitialization.reason: ensurePersistedQueuesOpen opens/upgrades database, binds stores, then immediately starts addon-deletion, key-share and message-resend drains.
Opening/init may upgrade schema and loadKeychain uses readwrite transaction, rotates expired keys.
onTransactionError for DecryptionError schedules a readwrite deletion of the corrupt entity or entire affected store. This is not a pure read-only export failure handler.
Default output redacts field values; not a complete data export.

migrationInference.possible: Known entities can in principle be decrypted with a captured source keychain/master and re-encrypted with a fresh destination master/keychain, without exporting the original nonextractable HKDF base key.
migrationInference.necessary: Rebuild all master-dependent primary/index hashes and ciphertext under a matching destination schema/keychain. Simply copying encrypted rows or old wrapped salts to a fresh master fails.
migrationInference.alternative: Rewrapping version salt under a fresh master while retaining clientKey/version preserves the derived content key, but primary/index hashes still require recomputation. This is a design inference, not tested code.
migrationInference.pendingActionRisk: A copied old queue row may trigger resend/key-share/deletion again when the official client opens. WAWebRecoverableQueue records before operation and acknowledges after; action and local acknowledgment are not one remote/local atomic transaction. Never label arbitrary queue replay harmless or silently omit queues while claiming a full archive.
migrationInference.completeArchiveBoundary: Need explicit queue snapshot/replay policy, consistent mutable Signal/application state, all supported schema branches, fresh key/salt bootstrap ordering, and actual independent restored-auth proof. This mapping resolves one encryption-format gap only.

nextSyntheticChecks: Owned generated source/destination masters and keychains; no provider APIs or real keys.
All four known schema shapes: numeric and hashed fields, preserved ordered queueId, ArrayBuffer/Uint8Array/BigInt/Set round trip.
Fresh destination ciphertext/nonces and hashes; source rows/keychain unchanged; cold reopen verifies semantic equality.
Wrong key/salt, tampered ciphertext, unsupported format/version/schema reject before destination commit.
Trap queue-drain/scheduler/network paths; never call ensurePersistedQueuesOpen for an export fixture.
Pending-queue replay requires its own design and tests; cryptographic round trip is not delivery-idempotency proof.
